title: Forerunner 965, 265, 265S: Everything to know about Garmin’s first AMOLED display-toting running watches in India
summary: Garmin has launched its first AMOLED display running watches in India, including the Forerunner 965, 265, and 265S. These watches offer extensive tracking features for runners and triathletes, with the 965 boasting advanced mapping and longer battery life. The prices are Rs 67,490 for the Forerunner 965 and Rs 50,490 for the 265 series, and they are available both online and offline.

title: Restaurant Brands earnings beats estimates, fueled by Tim Hortons' and Burger King's strong sales
summary: Restaurant Brands International exceeded Q1 earnings and revenue estimates, driven by double-digit same-store sales growth at Tim Hortons and Burger King. Burger King's U.S. same-store sales climbed 8.7%, indicating a successful turnaround, while Tim Hortons saw a 13.8% increase, especially strong in Canada. Popeyes also contributed with 5.6% same-store sales growth, and Firehouse Subs grew by 6.1%.

title: 3M laying off 1,100 at Maplewood headquarters
summary: 3M is laying off 1,100 employees at its Maplewood headquarters, which represents 10% of its local workforce and is part of a larger global cost-cutting initiative. This follows an earlier announcement of 6,000 global job cuts and an additional 2,500 manufacturing job reductions, bringing the total workforce reduction to 10% worldwide. Economists suggest these layoffs signal broader economic impacts from the Fed's interest rate hikes and changes in fiscal stimulus.

title: Keysight Highlights Challenges, Opportunities in Satellite Industry
summary: Keysight Technologies commissioned a survey revealing software test automation as a top challenge in the satellite industry, alongside the shift from large GEO to smaller LEO satellites due to reduced launch costs. The article discusses how automation in design-to-manufacturing and operational control systems can address these challenges, driven by a "gold rush" mentality and shortened development cycles. Keysight aims to support customers throughout the satellite lifecycle, from design to operations, through various testing, emulation, and simulation tools.

title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna warns employees who work remotely: 'Your career does suffer'
summary: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna stated that while he is not forcing employees back to the office, those who work remotely may find their careers suffering, particularly regarding promotions into managerial roles. He emphasized that in-person interaction is beneficial for career development and that remote work is best suited for specific individual contributor roles. Krishna's comments contribute to the ongoing debate about the merits of remote versus in-person work, with IBM encouraging employees to come into the office three days a week.

title: 40 Under 40: Champions of Construction 2022
summary: This article celebrates Autodesk's 40 Under 40: Champions of Construction for 2022, highlighting 40 individuals who are making significant contributions to the construction industry through innovation, leadership, and digital transformation. It details their roles, achievements, and impact on their respective companies and the broader AEC sector. The honorees are recognized for advancing digital maturity, implementing new technologies, and fostering collaborative and sustainable practices.

title: DXC Technology migrates insurance marketplace Lloyd’s to new data center
summary: DXC Technology has successfully migrated Lloyd's, the insurance marketplace, to a new, more modern data center as part of Lloyd's 'Blueprint Two' modernization strategy. This complex migration involved moving 70 billion rows of data, 700 IT assets, and over 200 mission-critical applications from a 40-year-old mainframe environment. The move, which took place over a single weekend in February, involved extensive planning and collaboration with over a dozen partners to minimize disruption.

title: Amazon class action alleges Prime subscribers pay false discount prices
summary: Amazon is facing a class action lawsuit alleging that its advertised Amazon Prime discounts are not genuine. The plaintiff claims that Amazon inflates original prices to create the appearance of a discount, thereby misleading consumers. The lawsuit seeks damages for affected customers and alleges violations of FTC guidelines regarding price comparisons.

title: Amazon Prime Subscribers Do Not Get the ‘Exclusive Savings’ They’re Promised, Class Action Alleges [DISMISSED]
summary: A class action lawsuit alleging that Amazon Prime subscribers do not receive promised "exclusive savings" has been dismissed. The judge ruled that the plaintiff failed to demonstrate how Amazon broke its promise or that he incurred damages, noting he did receive a discount on a television. The lawsuit claimed Amazon used "fictitious" strike-through prices by artificially raising product prices before applying "discounts" for Prime members.

title: Goop, Lemme Among Co. Hit With FTC Notices Over Marketing
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has issued notices to over 600 companies, including Goop and Kourtney Kardashian’s Lemme, Inc., warning them against making unsubstantiated product claims. The FTC stresses the importance of reliable evidence for marketing claims, particularly regarding health or safety benefits, and threatens civil penalties up to $50,120 per violation for deceptive practices. This action follows a Supreme Court decision limiting the FTC's ability to seek equitable monetary relief, prompting the agency to use penalty offense authority as an alternative enforcement tool.

title: Promotional home environment dinks Cornerstone Brand sales
summary: Qurate Retail Inc.'s Cornerstone division experienced a 13% decline in revenue to $297 million in Q1 due to an increasingly promotional environment for home goods and reduced average selling prices. The QxH division (QVC U.S. and HSN) also saw a 5% revenue decline, attributed to fewer customers and weakened consumer sentiment. The company is implementing initiatives to reactivate customer groups, but expects the impact to take several quarters to materialize.

title: Hanumakonda: KTR inaugurates 4 new companies; IT sector hired 1.5L people last year
summary: Telangana's IT and Industries Minister K.T. Rama Rao inaugurated four new IT companies in Hanamkonda (LTI Mindtree, Genpact, HRH Next, and Hexad Solutions Pvt. Ltd.), encouraging local youth for employment and entrepreneurship. Hyderabad continues to be a major IT hub, attracting global companies and adding over 1.5 lakh jobs in 2021-22, with plans to expand IT growth to other districts like Mahabubnagar, Siddipet, Nizamabad, and Nalgonda. The state government's policy framework, infrastructure, and human capital access have made Hyderabad a preferred destination for IT companies.

title: Cantaloupe Launches Smart Technology for Grab And Go at Self-Service Environments
summary: Cantaloupe Inc. has launched Cantaloupe Go, a new line of self-service apps and kiosks that utilize artificial intelligence for purchases in self-service retail locations and micro-markets. The technology allows consumers to unlock coolers or micro-markets and pay for items using a mobile app or kiosk, with AI and sensors tracking purchases. Cantaloupe Go is designed for flexibility in various environments, including food and beverage vending, and can be customized with convenience items.

title: Is the Market Reacting Too Negatively to Pinterest Earnings?
summary: Pinterest's stock tumbled 25% despite beating Q1 2023 top and bottom-line estimates and growing monthly active users (MAUs). The sell-off was primarily driven by concerns over slowing growth, rising operating expenses (opex), and a GAAP net loss of $209 million due to restructuring charges. While analysts remain cautiously optimistic with reiterations, several lowered price targets, reflecting market uncertainty regarding the company's profitability amidst its strategic restructuring efforts.

title: CEO pay continues to soar – new study
summary: A new study by Equilar reveals that median CEO pay at top US public companies increased by 7.7% to a record $22.3 million in 2022, despite negative S&P 500 returns. This rise was primarily driven by stock awards, leading to a median "pay ratio" of 288 times the median employee's compensation, significantly outpacing the 3.6% increase in average US private sector employee earnings. The study highlights a trend of incentivizing executives through substantial stock awards during uncertain economic times.

title: From stores to suppliers, how Destination XL tries to dodge the inventory ‘kiss of death’
summary: Destination XL (DXL) is strategically managing its inventory to avoid overstocking, a common pitfall in retail, by adopting a philosophy of "chasing goods rather than chasing cancellations." The company leverages AI and machine learning for efficient inventory management and has reduced its inventory relative to 2019 levels while increasing turnover. DXL is also diversifying its sourcing geographically, increasing production from Western hemisphere countries like Mexico and Nicaragua, and minimizing reliance on China, while maintaining a finite supplier base to build deeper relationships.

title: IonQ Appoints Pat Tang as VP of Research & Development
summary: IonQ, a quantum computing leader, announced the appointment of Pat Tang as Vice President of Research and Development. Tang, previously an Engineering Vice President at Amazon Lab126 and a team lead at Apple, will lead the company's technical exploration with a focus on developing impactful technologies for IonQ's systems. His extensive experience in building and scaling innovative technologies is expected to be invaluable as IonQ continues to advance quantum computing.

title: GlobalFoundries taps former Amazon exec for CFO seat
summary: GlobalFoundries has appointed former Amazon executive Tim Stone as its new Chief Financial Officer, replacing David Reeder. Stone brings extensive experience from Amazon and previous CFO roles at Snap, Ford Motor, and ASAPP. This leadership change comes as GlobalFoundries reported a 5% year-over-year revenue decline in its first quarter, though the company sees continued growth in markets like automotive and industrial IoT despite broader semiconductor industry challenges.

title: Dillard’s Shoppers Bought Shoes, Cosmetics and Women’s Clothing in Q1
summary: Dillard's Inc. surpassed Wall Street's expectations in Q1 despite a decline in sales and net income, driven by strong performance in cosmetics, shoes, and women's apparel. The company's retail gross margin was 45.6 percent, and operating expenses rose slightly. Analysts suggest that while Dillard's performed well given tough comparisons, the broader retail sector faces challenges due to a pressured middle class and increased spending on experiences.

title: Flush With Federal Money, Strings Attached, a Deep South Factory Votes to Unionize (Published 2023)
summary: Workers at Blue Bird, a Georgia factory producing electric school buses under federal subsidy, voted to unionize with the United Steelworkers. This victory marks a significant win for organized labor and Democrats, who hope federal clean-energy funding will bolster union presence in the South. This is the first major organizing election at a factory receiving federal funds under recent Biden administration legislation aimed at stimulating clean energy and supporting unions.

title: One Giant Leap for Brand Kind
summary: Companies are increasingly engaging in space marketing by placing product logos on spacecraft and conducting stunts in space to promote their brands. This trend is driven by the era of space capitalism and regulatory changes allowing private companies to participate in space missions, offering new revenue streams for financially risky ventures. While some express concern that this commercialization might diminish the sense of wonder surrounding space, brands like Columbia Sportswear believe it can highlight their innovative capabilities and garner publicity, even for failed missions.

title: George Soros bet on railroads, fitness, gig economy and lightened load on Disney, Amazon, dumped Tesla
summary: Soros Fund Management made new investments in railroad operators CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp., and the gig economy during the first quarter. The fund also adjusted its holdings in the media sector and divested from electric-vehicle maker Tesla Inc. These railroad investments occurred amidst ongoing labor tensions and increased scrutiny over safety in the industry.

title: Layoffs may cause organizational drag: Gartner
summary: According to Gartner research, layoffs can negatively impact shareholder returns within three years by leading to reduced employee morale, increased turnover, and loss of customers, despite initial cost savings. The report highlights that businesses often face immediate costs like severance payments and long-term issues such as higher contractor costs and demands for increased compensation from remaining staff. Gartner suggests alternative cost-cutting measures like voluntary reduced hours, executive pay cuts, hiring freezes, and internal redeployment to avoid "organizational drag."

title: Launch of first TiVo-based TVs delayed to second half of 2023
summary: The launch of the first TiVo-based connected TVs, manufactured by Vestel, has been delayed from spring to the second half of 2023, aligning with the holiday buying season. Despite this delay, Xperi, TiVo's parent company, maintains its revenue guidance for the year and announced a second "top 10" connected TV OEM partner for the European market, with product shipments expected in 2024. Xperi aims to expand this into a global business, emphasizing an independent, unbiased media platform in the competitive smart TV market.

title: Opal Fuels Sees Heavy-Duty Trucking Bulking RNG Demand
summary: Opal Fuels Inc., a major renewable natural gas (RNG) producer and distributor, is expanding its production projects to meet growing demand for RNG as a transportation fuel, particularly from the heavy-duty trucking sector. The company has secured long-term contracts with major corporations like Amazon.com Inc. and UPS, and is developing new landfill-based RNG facilities. Despite a decrease in first-quarter revenue due to holding back renewable identification number (RIN) sales following a drop in RIN prices, Opal Fuels remains optimistic about the future of RNG in the heavy-duty fuel market, projecting significant growth by 2030 and beyond.

title: Cable One® Teams with eero to Launch Advanced Whole-Home Connectivity Solution
summary: Cable One® announced the launch of Wall-To-Wall WiFi, an advanced whole-home connectivity solution, in collaboration with eero, an Amazon company. This service utilizes eero Pro6E and Wi-Fi 6 technology with patented TrueMesh to provide fast, reliable, and secure internet coverage throughout the home, eliminating dead zones and supporting over 100 connected devices simultaneously. The offering includes advanced online security features, parental controls, and an eero Plus option for additional protection.

title: Galileo Financial Technologies Joins AWS Marketplace
summary: Galileo Financial Technologies, a leading fintech company owned by SoFi Technologies, announced its solutions are now available on AWS Marketplace. This move aims to provide clients with innovative and accessible financial technology solutions, streamlining procurement and billing processes while offering Galileo's powerful API platform for card issuing and payment processing. The offerings include transaction processing, a payment risk platform, and conversational AI technology Cyberbank Konecta.

title: Amazon Bulls, Take Note: The Company's Improving Its Operations
summary: Amazon's stock is up 29% for the year due to improvements in its operations, particularly its delivery network, which has cut costs and shipment times. The company plans to expand same-day delivery centers to further enhance efficiency and profitability. Traders can leverage Amazon's performance using specialized ETFs like AMZU for bullish bets and AMZD for bearish positions.

title: Cognizant Strengthens its Global Delivery Network with New Innovation Hub in Malaysia
summary: Cognizant has opened a new regional innovation hub in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, aiming to strengthen its global delivery network and expand its talent pool to 5,000 employees by 2026. This hub features Cognizant’s first ASEAN Innovation Experience Lab and Centres of Excellence, including a Global Quality Engineering and Assurance Centre and an AWS Centre of Excellence, to provide innovative digital solutions to clients. Malaysian officials highlighted the investment as a testament to Malaysia's business environment and its role as a digital hub for ASEAN.

title: A2Z Smart Technologies Corp. announces formation of dedicated Big Data team
summary: A2Z Smart Technologies Corp. has formed a dedicated Big Data team to develop tools for identifying, mining, and collecting data from its Cust2Mate smart cart platform. This initiative aims to monetize data-based services as a significant revenue source. Additionally, A2Z announced a new partnership with HaStok Concept, an Israeli home design chain, expanding its smart cart solution into a new retail vertical.

title: Aramark Sports + Entertainment Announces Latest Innovation with Launch of New Amazon One Age Verification Capability at Coors Field
summary: Aramark Sports + Entertainment has announced the launch of a new Amazon One age verification capability at Coors Field. This innovation aims to streamline the purchasing process for age-restricted products, enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. The integration signifies Aramark's commitment to leveraging technology for improved service delivery in sports and entertainment venues.

title: What you need to know about Temu, the online shopping app dominating download charts
summary: Online shopping app Temu, owned by Chinese company PDD Holdings Inc., has quickly risen to popularity in Canada with its aggressive marketing, low prices, and gamified shopping experience. While it offers bargain deals, experts caution consumers about product quality, potential environmental impact from shipping and returns, and data privacy concerns given its sister app's issues. The platform's "growth-at-all-costs" approach and referral schemes are disrupting the e-commerce market, leading to a "race to the bottom" that could hurt local businesses.

title: Is BULZ Stock a buy?
summary: The article discusses BULZ, the ticker symbol for the MicroSectors FANG & Innovation 3X Leveraged ETNs, which trades on NYSE Arca. It explains that BULZ is an unsecured debt security providing leveraged exposure to the Solactive FANG Innovation Index, tracking 15 large-cap US tech stocks, and is not suitable for "buy and hold" investments. The article also mentions Bank of Montreal as the issuer and highlights Barclays' recent decision to redeem some of its own ETNs due to past issues, noting this does not directly impact BULZ but provides context on the ETN market.

title: Japan Airlines
summary: Japan Airlines (JAL) partnered with IBM Consulting to digitally transform its financial systems using SAP S/4HANA, overcoming pandemic challenges with a 100% remote deployment. This modernization allowed JAL to enhance operational efficiency, streamline processes, and gain deeper financial insights, despite significant market disruption. The project resulted in a 60% reduction in SAP customizations and improved financial reporting and analysis capabilities.

title: Invesco BulletShares 2031 Corporate Bond ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:BSCV)
summary: The Invesco BulletShares 2031 Corporate Bond ETF (BSCV) invests primarily in investment-grade corporate bonds maturing in 2031, aiming to return capital and proceeds to investors upon unwinding in December 2031. The ETF, managed by Invesco, had assets under management of $1.59 billion and a dividend yield of 4.60% as of the article's publication. Its shares have seen a slight increase year-to-date and its top holdings include major corporations like Verizon, Oracle, and Amazon.

title: TUG Top Holdings List & Exposure (STF Tactical Growth ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings for the STF Tactical Growth ETF (TUG), highlighting its significant exposure to technology companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft. It also breaks down TUG's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposures, showing a strong concentration in the United States and the technology sector, particularly in semiconductors. The fund is described as a multi-asset allocation fund focusing on North America.

title: Amazon Drivers Avoid Arbitration Claiming Non-delivery of Updated TOS
summary: The Ninth Circuit denied Amazon's motion to compel arbitration in a case brought by Amazon Flex drivers, ruling that the 2016 Terms of Service (TOS) applied instead of the 2019 version. Amazon failed to prove it provided adequate notice of the updated 2019 TOS and that there was mutual assent to its arbitration agreement. This decision highlights the importance for companies to ensure broad arbitration provisions and maintain records of notice for TOS updates.

title: In The Multicloud World, The Data’s The Thing
summary: Dell is expanding its Apex as-a-service portfolio, particularly focusing on data as the immutable center of the multicloud environment. The company emphasizes that while applications are ephemeral, data persistence and accessibility across various public and on-premises clouds are crucial for enterprises. Dell is positioning its storage-as-a-service offerings as a "Switzerland" for data, enabling organizations to achieve data gravity and avoid vendor lock-in, a strategy that executive John Roese states is paying off and differentiating Dell from competitors.

title: Activist firm Jana eyes boardroom fight at Freshpet
summary: Activist investor Jana Partners, the largest shareholder in pet food company Freshpet, wants to replace four board members to improve capital expenditure supervision and position the company for a potential sale. Jana, which owns a 9.3% stake, criticized the board for failing to oversee management and allowing performance to decline. Freshpet's shares have experienced significant volatility, and Jana's push comes amidst consolidation in the pet food industry.

title: ETF of the Week: Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP)
summary: VettaFi’s Tom Lydon discusses the Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP) which offers exposure to top holdings favored by hedge funds without an overweight toward any single stock. GVIP provides diversification across various companies, including some mid-cap and international stocks, making it a less volatile option for investors seeking innovative companies. It provides a consensus of top companies chosen by leading hedge fund managers, appealing to investors looking for strong, well-vetted companies.

title: Local Bounti names new CEO in executive transition
summary: Local Bounti Corporation announced that Anna Fabrega, former Freshly CEO and Amazon executive, will become CEO of the company on June 5, 2023. Current Co-CEOs and Co-Founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to Senior Vice President of Strategy and Chief Technology Officer, respectively, while retaining their board seats. Fabrega brings over two decades of experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production, with a proven track record of scaling businesses, including leading Amazon Go.

title: New HP and Sonos Devices Accentuate the Ultimate Home Office Workstation
summary: This article reviews the HP E45c G5 DQHD Curved Monitor and Sonos Era 100 Speakers, highlighting how they enhance productivity in a home office setup. The author praises the monitor's ultrawide display and Device Bridge feature for seamless multi-system operation, and the Sonos speakers for their superior sound quality and easy integration. Both devices are presented as valuable investments for improving the efficiency and enjoyment of hybrid work environments.

title: ETF of the Week: Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP)
summary: The Goldman Sachs Hedge Industry VIP ETF (GVIP) is highlighted as the ETF of the Week. GVIP provides exposure to top stock picks from hedge funds, focusing on a consensus of leading managers rather than an overweighting of individual stocks. The ETF diversifies holdings across large-cap, mid-cap, and international companies, offering a less volatile way for investors to participate in innovative companies.

title: US: Local Bounti appoints Anna Fabrega as CEO
summary: Local Bounti Corporation has announced the appointment of Anna Fabrega, formerly CEO of Freshly and an Amazon executive, as its new CEO, effective June 5, 2023. Current Co-CEOs and Co-Founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to strategic leadership roles within the company and remain on the Board of Directors. Fabrega brings extensive experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production, with a focus on scaling businesses and expanding market reach.

title: Local Bounti names new CEO
summary: Local Bounti Corp. has announced Anna Fabrega, former Freshly CEO and Amazon executive, will take over as CEO on June 5. The current co-CEOs and co-founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to senior leadership roles and retain their board seats. Fabrega brings over two decades of experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production to her new role at Local Bounti.

title: Local Bounti names new CEO
summary: Anna Fabrega, formerly CEO of Freshly and an Amazon executive, has been appointed as the new CEO of Local Bounti, effective June 5. The company's co-founders, Craig Hurlbert and Travis Joyner, will transition to senior vice president of strategy and chief technology officer, respectively, while retaining their board seats. Fabrega brings extensive experience in operations, consumer goods, and food production, with a focus on scaling businesses to drive Local Bounti's growth strategy.

title: Amazon Settles With FTC Over Claims Ring Doorbell Spies on Users (AMZN)
summary: Amazon has agreed to pay $30.8 million to settle two privacy cases with the Federal Trade Commission. One case involved allegations that Amazon's Ring video doorbells illegally spied on users, while the other concerned Alexa speakers collecting children's data without consent. The company will pay $5.8 million for the Ring complaint.

title: Netgear Nighthawk M6 Pro Wi-Fi Router Review
summary: The Netgear Nighthawk M6 Pro is a high-performance mobile Wi-Fi router supporting 5G mobile broadband and Wi-Fi 6E, making it suitable for business travelers and remote work. Despite its versatility and robust features like a 13-hour battery life and a 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port, its high price and somewhat unclear initial setup documentation are notable drawbacks. This review highlights its compact design, strong performance, and ability to switch between networking modes, positioning it as a top-tier but expensive solution for connectivity on the go.

title: Apple Bets On The Emerging Markets Growth Story
summary: Apple is increasingly focusing on emerging markets, particularly India, to drive growth amidst a challenging global smartphone market. The company achieved marginal growth in iPhone sales despite overall industry decline, with India seeing significant retail and manufacturing expansion plans. While services and financial technology offer long-term opportunities, the emerging markets strategy is a key component of Apple's immediate growth narrative, alongside ongoing share repurchases and dividend increases.

title: Salesforce shares drop on slowest revenue growth in more than 10 years
summary: Salesforce Inc (CRM.N) shares dropped about 7% after the company reported its slowest quarterly revenue growth in over 10 years, attributing it to companies cutting back on cloud-based software spending amid an uncertain U.S. economy and weaker demand. Despite the slowdown, analysts remained largely positive, citing Salesforce's push into AI and improved profitability as factors for future growth, leading to several price target increases.

title: Vimeo is tuning out its streaming TV apps
summary: Vimeo is discontinuing its dedicated streaming TV apps for Apple TV, Android TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Roku starting June 27th. Users can still watch Vimeo content on their TVs by casting from the Vimeo mobile app via Apple AirPlay 2 or Google Chromecast. This move aligns with Vimeo's strategic shift in recent years from a consumer-facing streaming destination to focusing on video-streaming services for businesses.

title: Microsoft Inks Deal With NVIDIA-Backed CoreWeave
summary: Microsoft has signed a deal with NVIDIA-backed cloud-computing startup CoreWeave, planning to invest billions to bolster its cloud computing infrastructure for AI operations. This partnership will provide Microsoft easier access to NVIDIA’s GPUs, which are crucial for AI-based applications like ChatGPT, and aims to give Microsoft a competitive edge against rivals like Alphabet Inc. and Amazon Web Services. CoreWeave’s access to over 45,000 GPUs and its status as an elite CSP in the NVIDIA Partner Network positions it as a key enabler for Microsoft's AI endeavors.

title: Introducing Apple Vision Pro: Apple’s first spatial computer
summary: Apple has unveiled Apple Vision Pro, its first spatial computer, which blends digital content with the physical world using a three-dimensional user interface controlled by eyes, hands, and voice. Running on the new visionOS, Vision Pro features an ultra-high-resolution display system, custom Apple silicon, and offers new ways to interact with apps, enjoy entertainment, relive memories, and connect via FaceTime. The device is designed with advanced materials, focuses on privacy, and will be available early next year starting at $3,499 (U.S.).

title: Is Walmart Stock a Buy, Sell, or Fairly Valued After Earnings?
summary: Morningstar maintains that Walmart (WMT) is fairly valued after its solid first-quarter earnings, raising its fair value estimate to $152 per share. The company's wide economic moat is attributed to its scale and cost advantage, allowing it to compete effectively in the evolving retail landscape. While facing an intensely competitive environment and economic uncertainty, Walmart's omnichannel strategy and value proposition are expected to drive continued growth.

title: C.H. Robinson’s New CEO Brings Experience From Ford, Amazon
summary: Dave Bozeman, an executive from Ford Motor Co. and formerly Amazon, has been named the new CEO of C.H. Robinson Worldwide, effective June 26. He replaces interim CEO Scott Anderson, who stepped in after Bob Biesterfeld's departure. Bozeman takes the helm during a challenging period for the global logistics provider, which has seen significant revenue decline and workforce reductions amid softening market conditions.

title: How Microsoft Fabric aims to beat Amazon and Google in the cloud war
summary: Microsoft has launched Fabric, a new cloud data and analytics platform designed to consolidate and simplify data management and analysis for enterprises. Analysts believe Fabric offers Microsoft a significant advantage over competitors like Amazon and Google by unifying disparate tools into a single platform with OneLake, a single data lake. This integration aims to reduce complexity, lower costs, and improve data quality, addressing key pain points for customers and potentially leapfrogging other cloud providers in enterprise analytics.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market to Open in Downtown Sarasota
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market is set to open a new 23,000-square-foot store in downtown Sarasota's upcoming Aster & Links complex, developed by Belpointe REIT Inc. This expansion signifies Sprouts' commitment to Florida, with new locations also planned for Bradenton and Fort Myers. The complex will feature residential units, retail space, and parking, replacing the former Main Plaza.

title: C.H. Robinson Appoints Dave Bozeman as CEO
summary: C.H. Robinson Worldwide has appointed former Amazon and Ford Motor Co. executive Dave Bozeman as its new CEO, effective June 26. Bozeman brings extensive experience in supply chain, transportation, and manufacturing, having previously served leadership roles at Amazon.com Inc. and Ford. He replaces interim CEO Scott Anderson, who will continue as a board member after the transition.

title: The 2023 Fortune 500 has been revealed: See which 9 Northeast Ohio companies made the list
summary: Nine Northeast Ohio companies made the prestigious 2023 Fortune 500 list, ranked by revenue for the 2022 fiscal year, with Mayfield Village-based Progressive Corporation being the highest-ranked local company at No. 88. The revenue threshold for making the list this year was $7.2 billion, a 13% increase from 2022. Several companies saw shifts in their rankings, with many increasing their revenue despite some dropping places on the list.

title: Cisco debuts its Secure Service Edge offering and enhances app security
summary: Cisco Systems Inc. has unveiled a new Secure Service Edge (SSE) offering called Cisco Secure Access, designed to help enterprises securely connect edge resources with features like zero-trust network access. Alongside SSE, Cisco announced Multicloud Defense for protecting cloud service workloads and significant upgrades to Panoptica, its cloud-native security development platform. These introductions aim to simplify security processes, enhance performance, and provide comprehensive protection across various enterprise environments.

title: People News: C.H. Robinson, Port NOLA
summary: C.H. Robinson has appointed Dave Bozeman as its new CEO and a member of its Board of Directors, effective June 26, 2023. Concurrently, Port NOLA announced Matthew Wypski as its new COO, succeeding Mike Stolzman. Both new appointees bring extensive experience from industry-leading companies to their respective roles.

title: Salesforce CEO Benioff shakes up executive team with new hires
summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff has announced significant changes to the company's executive management team, including new hires for chief revenue officer and chief marketing officer. This shakeup occurs six months after the departure of co-CEO Bret Taylor and follows recent layoffs impacting 10% of Salesforce's global workforce. The changes aim to address challenges highlighted by Benioff, including a difficult economic environment and questions about new hire productivity.

title: 2 Alabama-based companies make the Fortune 500
summary: Two Birmingham-based companies, Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, have been included in Fortune's 2023 list of the nation's largest corporations. Regions Financial ranked 483rd with $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan Materials placed 494th with over $7.3 billion in revenue. The Fortune 500 list, which ranks companies by their 2022 fiscal year revenue, features 52 companies led by women CEOs, an all-time high.

title: C.H. Robinson appoints Dave Bozeman as CEO
summary: C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc. has appointed Dave Bozeman as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective June 26, 2023. Bozeman, an executive with over 30 years of experience from companies like Ford and Amazon, will also join the Board of Directors. Scott Anderson, the interim CEO, will ensure a smooth transition and remain on the board.

title: Revolutionizing cloud spending: How ProsperOps' AI solution is curbing public cloud expenses
summary: ProsperOps, a company founded by ex-Rackspace Technology Inc. employees, has developed an AI-enabled automation platform to reduce public cloud expenses. Erik Carlin, co-founder and chief product officer, explained that their platform moves beyond simple recommendations to actively optimize cloud environments, saving customers money. The company aims to tackle the significant issue of waste in public cloud spending, estimated at around $24 billion for AWS alone.

title: Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF
summary: This page provides a comprehensive guide to the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RSPD), including its stock quote, holdings, and various performance metrics. It details the ETF's profile, such as its issuer, expense ratio, inception date, and the index it tracks, alongside comparing its valuation, dividends, and expenses to peer ETFs. The article also covers RSPD's ESG scores, real-time ratings, performance returns, geographic and sector exposure, and technical analysis data.

title: Apple, Amazon must face consumer lawsuit over iPhone, iPad prices, US judge rules
summary: A federal judge in Seattle has ruled that Apple and Amazon must face a consumer antitrust lawsuit accusing them of conspiring to artificially inflate the price of iPhones and iPads sold on Amazon's platform. The lawsuit alleges that a 2019 agreement between the two companies restricted the number of competitive resellers, a claim that will now proceed to evidence-gathering. Apple contends the agreement was to minimize counterfeit goods and is procompetitive.

title: A breakdown of AI ETFs as tech names burn bright
summary: This article breaks down various AI-focused ETFs available in Europe, examining their methodologies, holdings, and performance. It highlights the differences in how these ETFs define and capture the AI theme, from market-cap weighted exposure to companies involved in big data and NLP to equally-weighted exposure based on AI-related revenue or IP. The piece also compares their costs, liquidity, and correlation of returns, noting that while some are dominated by large tech names, others offer differentiated exposure to companies leveraging machine learning.

title: Regions Financial, Vulcan Materials make Fortune 500
summary: Two Birmingham-based companies, Regions Financial and Vulcan Materials, have been named to the Fortune 500 list, ranking 483rd and 494th respectively. Regions generated $7.5 billion in revenue, while Vulcan amassed $7.3 billion during the 2022 fiscal period. Vulcan Materials was also recognized as one of the top 200 Best Companies to Work For by U.S. News and World Report.

title: Silicon Labs' FG28 Integrates Dual-Band Sub-GHz / BLE Radio with Machine Learning Accelerator
summary: Silicon Labs has unveiled the FG28, a new dual-band system-on-a-chip (SoC) that combines a sub-GHz radio and an AI/ML accelerator, making it the first of its kind. The FG28 features an Arm Cortex-M33 core, memory, and a Matrix Vector Processor for on-device AI/ML applications, alongside both sub-GHz for long-range and 2.4 GHz Bluetooth Low-Energy for local communication. It supports protocols like Amazon Sidewalk and Wi-SUN, with samples currently available and general availability expected by Q3 2023.

title: Additions to Fortinet FortiFlex deliver more flexible licensing options to customers
summary: Fortinet Inc. has introduced new product and service additions to its FortiFlex program, offering customers more flexible licensing options, including support for physical FortiGate next-generation firewall appliances. The program, which uses a points system for usage-based pricing, is now available via private offer in the Amazon Web Services Inc. Marketplace. FortiFlex aims to address the evolving needs of highly distributed networks by allowing organizations to pay by usage and manage licenses more efficiently across various deployment types.

title: Satellite Broadband Provider Viasat Acquired Inmarsat for $7.3 Billion – Now What?
summary: Viasat completed its $7.3 billion acquisition of Inmarsat, creating a global communications provider that combines their complementary technology assets, resources, and service portfolios. The merger aims to offer customers enhanced speed, bandwidth, reliability, and broader coverage through a multi-layered network incorporating Ka-, L-, and S-band spectrums. This integration positions the combined entity to capitalize on the growing direct-to-device and multi-orbit 5G mobile markets in satellite communications.

title: Andy Eccles: CDW Expands Public Sector Cloud Business Through Enquizit Acquisition
summary: CDW has acquired Enquizit, an Amazon Web Services cloud services provider specializing in the public sector, to enhance its IT offerings for government and education markets. The acquisition, which CDW expects to have no material impact on its 2023 financial performance, will boost CDW's Digital Velocity practice with Enquizit's cloud transformation, application modernization, and cybersecurity capabilities, including its AI-based SkyMap platform. Andy Eccles, SVP of integrated technology solutions at CDW, noted how Enquizit's expertise aligns with CDW's strategic goals.

title: Uber Eats to Deploy 2,000 Autonomous Robots from Serve Robotics
summary: Uber Eats is partnering with Serve Robotics to deploy 2,000 autonomous delivery robots, aiming to reduce delivery costs and increase efficiency. These robots navigate city environments with Level 4 autonomy using AI, LiDAR, ultrasonic transducers, and cameras. While the move offers significant technical advantages, it also raises societal questions about job displacement and ethical considerations in the expanding field of autonomous logistics.

title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison confirms new gen AI service with Cohere during earnings call
summary: Oracle is partnering with Cohere to launch a new generative AI cloud service that will allow enterprises to train customized large language models (LLMs) using their private data while ensuring privacy and security. Oracle founder Larry Ellison announced the collaboration during the company's Q4 earnings call, highlighting Oracle's existing role in AI development and its significant investment in Cohere. This initiative expands Oracle's offerings in the rapidly growing generative AI market, where it competes with other major cloud providers.

title: AMD launches new Instinct MI300X AI chip to take on Nvidia’s GPUs
summary: AMD has launched its new Instinct MI300X AI accelerator chip, designed to compete with Nvidia's GPUs in the generative AI market. The company also introduced its Infinity Architecture Platform, powered by eight MI300X chips, and its ROCm software ecosystem. Despite these announcements, AMD's stock fell due to a lack of major customer endorsements for the new chips and details on pricing.

title: AMD's AI chip challenge to Nvidia remains uphill fight with no big customers named
summary: AMD unveiled new details about its MI300X artificial intelligence chip, designed to challenge Nvidia's market dominance, but did not announce any major customers for the product. While the chip offers significant memory capacity aimed at cost reduction for AI services, the lack of customer commitments disappointed Wall Street, causing AMD's stock to fall. Analysts noted that Nvidia's strong market position is reinforced by its software ecosystem, which AMD is attempting to counter with its Rocm platform.

title: Grainger Leases 500K SF Warehouse at Carolina Logistics Park
summary: W.W. Grainger, Inc., an industrial supplier, has leased over 525,000 square feet of bulk warehouse space at Carolina Logistics Park in Pineville, NC. This facility will serve as a receiving, stocking, and shipping hub for Grainger and is expected to be operational in 2024. The Carolina Logistics Park, developed by Beacon Partners, also hosts tenants like Amazon and Carolina Foods.

title: Labor Ruling Offers Unionization Path to Uber, Lyft Drivers
summary: A recent U.S. labor board ruling has made it easier for workers to be classified as employees rather than independent contractors, potentially opening the door for unionization efforts among gig workers at companies like Uber and Lyft. While gig companies argue this could impact their business model, the decision emboldens organizing campaigns, despite the inherent difficulties in unionizing a dispersed workforce. This ruling could lead to significant challenges for gig companies, potentially forcing them to negotiate with unions, though hurdles remain for successful organizing drives.

title: Fidelity Disruptive Technology ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:FDTX)
summary: The Fidelity Disruptive Technology ETF (FDTX) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in innovative businesses with the potential for market disruption, including global disruptive technology companies in areas like machine learning and AI. The fund launched in April 2020 and is managed by Fidelity, with assets under management of $191.07 million. FDTX holdings include major tech companies such as NVIDIA, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Microsoft, and Amazon.com.

title: Sonos Era 300 Review: Spatial Audio Is a Game Changer
summary: The Sonos Era 300 is the company's first speaker designed specifically for spatial audio, aiming to revolutionize how we experience music beyond traditional stereo. While it boasts a unique design and offers good stereo performance with Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity, its key selling point is the immersive spatial audio experience, particularly with services like Amazon Music Unlimited and Apple Music. Although pricey at $449 and limited in spatial audio service support at launch, the Era 300 delivers impressive sound quality that justifies the investment, especially when considering its potential as rear surround speakers for a home theater setup.

title: Maximum Effort Channel, a Partnership Between Fubo and Ryan Reynolds’ Maximum Effort, Will Launch on Fubo, Amazon Freevee, LG Channels, Plex, Sling Freestream, VIDAA, VIZIO WatchFree+, Xumo Play
summary: FuboTV Inc. and Ryan Reynolds’ Maximum Effort announced that the "Maximum Effort Channel" will launch on June 20, 2023, across multiple platforms including Fubo, Amazon Freevee, and Sling Freestream. The channel will feature original and classic TV and movies, kicking off with "Bedtime Stories with Ryan." This launch is part of a multi-year partnership between Fubo and Maximum Effort, with Maximum Effort having creative control over the channel's content.

title: JD.com Announces “35711 Vision” for the Next Twenty Years
summary: JD.com unveiled its "35711 Vision" on its 20th anniversary, outlining ambitious goals for the next two decades focused on financial growth, societal impact, and sustainability. These goals include achieving significant revenue and profit targets, ranking multiple enterprises on the Fortune Global 500, creating numerous jobs, and contributing substantially to various societal and environmental initiatives. The vision is supported by strategic focuses on lower-tier markets, technology and services, and international business expansion.

title: Sensex, Nifty Decline As RIL, ICICI Bank Drag: Market Wrap
summary: India's benchmark stock indices, Sensex and Nifty, declined on Monday despite opening higher, primarily dragged down by heavyweight stocks like ICICI Bank Ltd. and Reliance Industries Ltd. The S&P BSE Sensex fell by 216 points, and the NSE Nifty 50 closed 71 points lower. This decline mirrored a cautious global market sentiment following a strong second-quarter rally in Wall Street that lost momentum.

title: Freehold Raceway Mall Sears deal: See what happened to other Jersey Shore Sears stores
summary: Macerich, the owner of Freehold Raceway Mall, has acquired full ownership of the former Sears building, making it easier to fill the 72,000-square-foot vacant lower level with new retail, entertainment, or restaurant uses. Other former Sears locations at the Jersey Shore have been redeveloped into various businesses, including an At Home store, an Amazon delivery station, new restaurants and shops, and a ShopRite supermarket complex. The article details how different malls and developers are adapting these large retail spaces.

title: Sonos Five review: is Sonos' biggest, priciest wireless speaker its best?
summary: The Sonos Five is reviewed as a solid wireless speaker, praised for its bold, expansive sound and multi-room potential within the Sonos ecosystem. While it delivers room-filling audio, the review notes it can be overly bassy and lacks Bluetooth, suggesting that the newer Era 300 offers a more refined and expressive sound despite the Five's louder output.

title: Spotify has higher-priced subscription plan in the pipeline: report
summary: Spotify is reportedly planning to introduce a higher-priced "Supremium" subscription tier that will offer high-fidelity audio and additional audiobooks. This new plan, which was previously delayed, is expected to roll out to non-U.S. users in 2023, with American users gaining access later. The company recently increased its monthly active users to 515 million and premium subscribers to 210 million in the first quarter, and also announced an AI DJ feature.

title: Minnesota firm acquires retail brokerage in Bentonville, strengthening connections with Walmart, Sam's Club
summary: Select Sales Inc., a Minnesota-based retail sales and marketing agency, has acquired Bentonville Merchants (BMI), a sales agency that specifically serves Walmart and Sam’s Club brands. This merger, announced on June 21, 2023, creates a new company designed to enhance connections between manufacturers and leading American retailers. The combined entity aims to leverage local market expertise and robust data-driven strategies to accelerate growth for both divisions and provide a comprehensive one-stop solution for manufacturers.

title: PLDT and CSG Build On 20-Year Relationship to Modernize for the Future
summary: PLDT, the Philippines' largest telco, is expanding its two-decade partnership with CSG (NASDAQ: CSGS) to modernize its business for the future, particularly for its Enterprise unit. This large-scale transformation involves adopting a cloud-based, unified billing and revenue management solution. The collaboration aims to streamline processes, minimize costs, shorten time to market, and enhance the customer experience for PLDT Enterprise customers.

title: Some ESG Issues Take Center Stage at Big Tech Investor Meetings
summary: ESG principles are increasingly important at big tech companies, with shareholder demands evolving beyond traditional environmental concerns to focus on social and governance issues. Recent investor meetings at Alphabet and Meta, both holdings in the Invesco ESG Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQMG), saw a rise in shareholder resolutions concerning online safety, gender/racial equity, human rights, and executive compensation. This trend highlights the growing emphasis on the "S" and "G" in ESG, potentially positioning QQMG as a relevant investment for those seeking exposure to mega-cap growth with an ESG focus.

summary: This article summarizes recent hedge fund and insider trading news, including BlueCrest Capital Management's court win against a compensation claim, Steve Cohen's $5 million donation for psychedelic research, losses faced by funds betting against Ocado, and a Citadel portfolio manager moving to Marshall Wace. title: The best buy now, pay later (BNPL) apps
summary: This article reviews the best Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) apps for consumers looking to finance purchases. It explains how BNPL services work, emphasizing interest-free installment plans for shorter terms and cautioning against higher APRs for longer plans. The article highlights Affirm, PayPal Pay with BNPL, Sezzle, Afterpay, and Klarna, detailing their features, merchant compatibility, and optimal use for managing larger expenses.

title: 'Millions of homeowners:' Frontdoor's branding to arrive on doorsteps through deal with Amazon
summary: Frontdoor has announced a partnership with Amazon, which will lead to its new app's branding appearing on customers' doorsteps as part of product deliveries. This collaboration aims to expose "millions of homeowners" to Frontdoor's offerings. The deal builds on Frontdoor's recent marketing efforts, including a national ad campaign featuring MLB star Ronald Acuña Jr.

title: The new Furby is here whether you like it or not
summary: Hasbro has launched a new generation of Furby, just in time for the original's 25th birthday, available now on Amazon for $69.99 and other retailers starting July 15. The revamped toy includes a microphone for voice commands, supports over 600 responses, and features a completely overhauled design. It can dance, tell fortunes, copy voices, perform light shows, and even lead meditation sessions.

title: SAIC wins $1.3B Treasury cloud contract
summary: Science Applications International Corp. (SAIC) has been awarded a $1.3 billion contract by the Department of the Treasury for cloud modernization. Under the T-Cloud contract, SAIC will act as a cloud broker, managing services from major cloud providers like Amazon, Google, IBM, Microsoft, and Oracle, supporting the Treasury's adoption of a multi-cloud environment. The contract, with a seven-year performance period, aims to enable rapid and secure adoption of modern cloud solutions and centralize management to reduce costs and duplicative efforts.

title: Amazon Is Spending $100 Million to Teach Cloud Customers About AI
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is investing $100 million in a new Generative AI Innovation Center. This initiative aims to help its cloud customers develop and deploy AI products, connecting them with AI and machine learning experts. The move positions Amazon to compete with Microsoft and Google in the rapidly expanding generative AI market, with early users including Highspot, Twilio, Ryanair, and Lonely Planet.

title: Amazon.com Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) stock rose 4.26% to $130.15 on Thursday, outperforming a mixed market day where the S&P 500 Index saw a slight gain and the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a minimal decline. The company's shares closed $16.42 below its 52-week high.

title: EBay creates event series for sports trading card collectors
summary: EBay has launched "Collectors Camp," an event series for sports trading card enthusiasts to learn about enhancing their collections. The initiative, guided by eBay seller David Prince and NBA player Mikal Bridges, will teach attendees how to use eBay's tools for buying, trading, and selling cards. This program is part of eBay's broader strategy to expand its sports memorabilia and collectibles market, which includes past efforts in authentication, the eBay Vault, and the acquisition of TCGplayer.

title: 7.5 Million 'Baby Shark' Bath Toys Recalled Due to Serious Injuries to Kids
summary: Nearly 8 million "Baby Shark" and "Mini Baby Shark" bath toys have been recalled after reports of serious injuries to children, including impalement and lacerations. The injuries occurred when children slipped or sat on the toys' hard plastic top fin. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the toys, disable them, and contact Zuru for a refund.
