CEO Jamie Iannone informed employees that the company will also reduce its alternate workforce contracts and highlighted the need for better organization and nimbleness.

title: eBay Stock Surges After Saying It Will Cut 9% of Its Workforce—Monitor These Key Levels
summary: eBay announced plans to cut 9% of its workforce, or 1,000 jobs, which led to a nearly 3% surge in its stock price. CEO Jamie Iannone stated that the company's headcount and expenses had outpaced business growth. The article also provides key technical levels for investors to monitor eBay's stock performance within a descending channel pattern.

title: Boeing’s history reveals connections and disconnections in the West’s economy
summary: This article examines Boeing's history to illustrate the evolving relationship between corporations and the communities they are rooted in. It highlights how Boeing's shifts, from its early growth in Seattle powered by government contracts and regional resources to its later decision to move headquarters and the recent 737 Max crisis, demonstrate a trend where corporate loyalty to specific locales diminishes. The author argues that this placelessness often creates an asymmetrical relationship, forcing communities to adapt to companies rather than the other way around.

title: Analog Devices Appoints Richard C. Puccio, Jr. as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
summary: Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI) announced the appointment of Richard C. Puccio, Jr. as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective February 5, 2024. Mr. Puccio, formerly CFO at Amazon Web Services (AWS) and a partner at PwC, will lead ADI's global finance operations and financial strategy. His extensive experience in technology sectors is expected to accelerate ADI's operational effectiveness and shareholder value.

title: Analog Devices finds permanent CFO from Amazon Web Services
summary: Analog Devices has appointed Richard Puccio, formerly CFO of Amazon Web Services, as its new permanent Chief Financial Officer. Puccio served as AWS's CFO for almost three years before joining the Wilmington-based semiconductor firm. This appointment follows previous reports regarding Analog Devices' search for a permanent CFO.

title: Analog Devices Appoints Richard C. Puccio, Jr. as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
summary: Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI) announced the appointment of Richard C. Puccio, Jr. as its new Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective February 5, 2024. Mr. Puccio, former CFO of Amazon Web Services (AWS) and a long-time partner at PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), will be responsible for ADI's financial strategy and global finance operations. CEO and Chair Vincent Roche highlighted Puccio's extensive experience in leading financial advisory and high-growth technology operations as a significant asset for ADI.

title: IonQ Achieves Technical Milestone One Year Ahead of Schedule
summary: IonQ announced it achieved its 35 algorithmic qubits (#AQ) technical milestone a full year ahead of schedule on its IonQ Forte system. This innovation enables larger and more sophisticated quantum circuits, making the systems more valuable for applications like quantum machine learning and chemistry. The company's CEO, Peter Chapman, highlighted this achievement as a testament to IonQ's technical leadership and aggressive roadmap in quantum computing.

title: Historic $10B planned investment to benefit Entergy Mississippi customers
summary: Entergy Mississippi announced a historic $10 billion investment by Amazon Web Services (AWS) in Mississippi will bring new jobs and economic development, while supporting long-term power reliability and affordability for all Entergy Mississippi customers. This significant capital investment, finalized by Mississippi lawmakers, is expected to help keep electricity rates lower and drive advancements in the power grid and generation across the state. Entergy Mississippi, which serves 461,000 customers in 45 counties, emphasized its readiness to support AWS and other growing companies, highlighting its century-long commitment to providing reliable power.

title: Amazon.com Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) stock rose 0.87% to $159.12 on Friday, marking its fourth consecutive day of gains. This performance occurred on a mixed trading day where the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) increased by 0.16% and the S&P 500 Index (SPX) fell by 0.07%. The article highlights Amazon's strong individual performance relative to broader market trends.

title: Salesforce slashes 700 jobs, adding to brutal string of 2024 tech layoffs
summary: Salesforce Inc. is reportedly laying off approximately 700 workers, continuing a trend of recent job cuts in the tech industry at the beginning of 2024. These layoffs affect less than 1% of its workforce and follow a 10% reduction a year prior, as the company focuses on cost-cutting and expanding profit margins under shareholder pressure. Other major tech firms like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have also announced layoffs this month.

title: Why Amazon.com Is in Trouble
summary: Amazon's e-commerce and Prime Video businesses are facing significant challenges from growing competition and slowing growth, despite revenue increases in recent quarters. While Amazon Web Services (AWS) continues to be robust with substantial operating profits, its growth is also slowing and is proving insufficient to fully offset the struggles of Amazon's legacy businesses. This creates a difficult situation for the company, as its faster-growing, larger-margin AWS may not be able to counteract these broader issues.

title: iRobot Announces Operational Restructuring Plan to Position Company for the Future
summary: iRobot Corporation announced an operational restructuring plan to stabilize the company and focus on profitability after the termination of its merger agreement with Amazon. The plan includes significant cost reductions, a workforce reduction of approximately 350 employees, and a leadership transition, with Colin Angle stepping down as CEO and Glen Weinstein appointed as Interim CEO. iRobot also provided preliminary fourth-quarter 2023 results, reporting an anticipated full-year revenue of $891 million and a GAAP operating loss between $265 million and $285 million.

title: Amazon taps Kueski for buy now, pay later service in Mexico
summary: Amazon Mexico has partnered with venture capital-backed fintech Kueski Inc. to offer a buy now, pay later service, Kueski Pay, allowing customers to pay in bi-weekly installments without needing a credit card. This initiative addresses the large unbanked population in Mexico and expands flexible payment options for Amazon customers. Kueski, a leading BNPL provider in Latin America, has secured over $300 million in funding for its services.

title: UFCW steps up efforts to stop Kroger-Albertsons merger
summary: The United Food and Commercial Workers International Union (UFCW) held a press conference to reiterate its opposition to the proposed Kroger-Albertsons merger, pushing back on claims made by the grocers. The union raised significant concerns about C&S Wholesale Grocers' ability to successfully manage the over 400 divested stores, citing a substantial decline in their revenue. The UFCW also expressed apprehension about C&S's corporate structure and its willingness to honor collective bargaining agreements.

title: US OPEN: SoFi Technologies rallies 15% on first quarterly profit
summary: SoFi Technologies (SOFI.US) rallied 15% after reporting its first profitable quarter since going public, with adjusted Q4 net revenue significantly exceeding expectations at $594.2 million and EPS at $0.02 against an expected loss. Despite strong Q4 results, the company provided a more conservative Q1 2024 outlook for adjusted net revenue and EBITDA. Meanwhile, other market news saw SoFi shares trading above the $8.00 resistance, while Amazon terminated its acquisition of iRobot, and Philips reported a significant miss in Q4 earnings and halted US sales of sleep apnea devices.

title: Amazon, Roomba-parent iRobot abandon $1.4 billion merger deal
summary: Amazon and iRobot have abandoned their $1.4 billion merger deal due to opposition from EU and U.S. antitrust regulators. iRobot announced a significant restructuring, including cutting 350 jobs and the stepping down of its CEO, Colin Angle, while Amazon will pay iRobot a $94 million termination fee. Regulators were concerned Amazon could use the acquisition to hinder iRobot's rivals on its online marketplace.

title: Amazon.com Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) shares dropped 1.40% on Tuesday, closing at $159.00, breaking a five-day winning streak. Despite this decline, the stock still outperformed the broader S&P 500 Index, which also saw a slight decrease, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose.

title: 2027 the Target for Transition Away from 1D GTIN, Toward Digital Link 2D Barcodes
summary: The packaging industry is targeting 2027 for a significant transition from the traditional 1D GTIN barcode to the more versatile Digital Link 2D barcode. This shift, driven by increasing consumer demand for information, regulatory requirements, and supply chain traceability needs, will enable a single QR code to provide different information to various stakeholders (consumers, retailers, supply chain partners). The "Sunrise 2027" program aims to prepare the necessary infrastructure, primarily software changes, for this industry-wide adoption.

title: Why global corporations are attracted to Palm Beach County, Florida
summary: Palm Beach County, Florida, is attracting numerous international corporations and financial institutions due to its diversified economy, top-notch educational and health care facilities, safety, and substantial tax benefits. The county also offers excellent location and transportation links, including a high-speed Brightline train, and has a strong economic development organization, the Business Development Board (BDB), supporting business growth.

title: Walmart plans to add more than 150 large-format stores across the U.S.
summary: Walmart plans to open more than 150 large-format stores, including conversions and new constructions, across the U.S. over the next five years. This expansion signals Walmart's commitment to its brick-and-mortar presence, despite growing online competition, and comes as the company continues to outperform other retailers by attracting a broader customer base. The new stores will feature a modern design with sustainability features and updated technology.

title: SellersFi, Amazon team up to offer up to $10M in credit lines
summary: SellersFi has partnered with Amazon Lending to provide credit lines of up to $10 million to eligible Amazon sellers, particularly targeting larger businesses with revenues exceeding $2.5 million annually. These credit lines are facilitated through Citi, which, alongside Fasanara Capital, provided a $300 million credit facility to SellersFi. The initiative addresses the challenges e-commerce businesses face in securing traditional financing, utilizing SellersFi's cash-flow-based underwriting to approve credit lines rapidly while allowing Amazon to retain sellers within its ecosystem.

title: IBM mandates managers back to the office; 3 days a week
summary: IBM has issued a new directive requiring all its managers in the U.S. to work from the office or client locations a minimum of three days a week, a policy change that could lead to job termination for non-compliance. Managers must reside within 50 miles of an IBM office and have until August to relocate or face separation from the company. This decision by IBM contradicts a previous statement from CEO Arvind Krishna and aligns with other tech companies enforcing in-person work.

title: Downtown Nashville is getting another music venue
summary: Developers have unveiled plans for a new 4,500-seat music venue called "The Pinnacle" coming to Nashville Yards in early 2025, with Pinnacle Financial Partners as the naming rights sponsor and AEG running operations. This addition will provide another large-scale ticketed live music option downtown, competing with existing venues like the Ryman and Bridgestone Arena. Pinnacle Financial Partners is also moving its headquarters to Nashville Yards.

title: Walmart announces ambitious 5-year growth plan
summary: Walmart has revealed an ambitious five-year growth plan, intending to build or convert over 150 new locations and remodel 650 existing stores within the next year. These efforts will incorporate Walmart's "Store of the Future" concept, focusing on improved layouts, expanded product selections, and innovative technology. The initiative aims to capitalize on Walmart's strong performance in the grocery sector and create tens of thousands of jobs across the country.

title: Plug Power Completes First Customer Fill of Liquid Green Hydrogen at its Georgia Plant
summary: Plug Power has successfully completed the first customer fill of liquid green hydrogen produced at its Woodbine, Georgia plant, with the hydrogen being transported to sites for Walmart, Amazon, and Home Depot. This milestone follows the official commencement of operations at the plant, which houses the largest proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer deployment in the U.S. The Georgia plant can produce up to 15 tons per day of liquid green hydrogen, demonstrating a significant step towards a cost-effective green hydrogen economy.

title: What companies experienced massive layoffs in 2024? Who's making cuts so far
summary: Several major companies have announced significant layoffs in early 2024, impacting various sectors from technology and retail to healthcare and airlines. Companies like UPS, Microsoft, Humana, eBay, American Airlines, Wayfair, Twitch, Google, Business Insider, and Sports Illustrated are reducing their workforces due to factors such as economic conditions, restructuring efforts, and changes in business strategies. These cuts range from hundreds to thousands of employees globally.

title: Sonos Era 100 vs. Era 300: Budget or brawn?
summary: This article compares the Sonos Era 100 and Era 300 smart speakers, highlighting their differences in price, size, features, and sound quality. The Era 100 is presented as a more budget-friendly option with excellent sound for most users, while the pricier Era 300 offers Dolby Atmos spatial audio and greater power for larger rooms or audiophiles. The decision between the two depends on budget, the importance of Dolby Atmos, and room size.

title: NEOS Nasdaq 100 High Income ETF
summary: This page provides comprehensive information on the NEOS Nasdaq 100 High Income ETF (QQQI), including its stock profile, dividends, expense ratio, holdings, ESG scores, and performance data as of April 3, 2026. QQQI is an actively managed large-cap blend equity ETF with an expense ratio of 0.68% and significant AUM of $9,433.8 million, showing strong fund flows over several periods. The ETF primarily invests in major technology companies and aims to provide high income, reflected in its substantial annual dividend yield of 16.04%.

title: Markets Brief: Will the ‘Magnificent Seven’ Stocks Keep Carrying the Market After Earnings?
summary: The article analyzes the performance of the "Magnificent Seven" stocks after their latest earnings reports, noting that while most beat forecasts, market reactions were mixed due to high expectations. It discusses whether these tech giants can continue to drive market gains in 2024, given their current valuations and the potential for a broader market rally. The article also provides a detailed recap of individual company performances and analyst commentary.

title: Apple, Skechers fall; Amazon, Deckers Outdoor rise, Friday, 2/2/2024
summary: On Friday, February 2, 2024, several major stocks experienced significant price changes. Apple and Skechers saw declines due to lukewarm forecasts, while Amazon, Deckers Outdoor, Meta Platforms, and Clorox rose following strong financial results or optimistic outlooks. Microchip Technology and Columbia Sportswear also faced drops after giving disappointing forecasts.

title: BofA’s Hartnett Says Stock Markets Are Behaving Like Dot-Com Era
summary: According to Bank of America strategists led by Michael Hartnett, the current rush into technology stocks mirrors the dot-com bubble of 1999. This market behavior suggests an expectation of a strong economy despite tighter monetary policy. The strategists note an unusual scenario where both Nasdaq and yields are rising, a price action typically seen post-recession.

title: Amazon’s Jeff Bezos Filed Plan to Sell Up to $8.6 Billion of Stock
summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has filed a plan to sell up to 50 million shares of Amazon stock by January 2025, which could amount to up to $8.6 billion. This marks his first planned stock sale in over two years. Bezos currently serves as the executive chair of the company.

title: Amazon Stock Jumps On Earnings Beat, Cloud AI Product Growth—Key Price Levels to Watch
summary: Amazon (AMZN) shares surged over 7% in premarket trading after reporting a strong quarterly earnings beat, driven by robust retail performance and increasing demand for its cloud division's AI products. CEO Andy Jassy highlighted the potential for generative AI services to generate tens of billions in revenue in the coming years. Analysts are watching key price levels, with the stock poised for a breakout from a rising wedge pattern and potential overhead resistance near all-time highs.

title: Crocs names CFO Anne Mehlman as President
summary: Crocs has appointed Anne Mehlman, its current EVP and Chief Financial Officer, as the new EVP & President, succeeding Michelle Poole who is retiring. Poole will remain in an advisory role until early 2025 to ensure a smooth transition. Mehlman brings over 20 years of experience and will continue as CFO until a replacement is found.

title: Exclusive | Intel Delays $20 Billion Ohio Project, Citing Slow Chip Market
summary: Intel is delaying its $20 billion chip-manufacturing project in Ohio, pushing the completion of its factories to late 2026. This delay is attributed to challenging market conditions and the slow distribution of U.S. government grants intended to boost the domestic semiconductor industry. The company's stock symbol is INTC.

title: Bezos plans on selling 50 million Amazon shares during next 12 months
summary: Jeff Bezos, the executive chair of Amazon, plans to sell up to 50 million shares of Amazon stock within the next year, according to a recent SEC filing. This prearranged trading plan, adopted in November, indicates sales will conclude by January 25 of next year. Bezos currently owns over 988 million Amazon shares, which constitute a significant portion of his substantial net worth.

title: Snap, the owner of Snapchat, is laying off about 10% of its global workforce
summary: Snap Inc., the company behind Snapchat, is reducing its global workforce by approximately 10%, impacting about 530 employees. This marks the latest in a series of layoffs for the tech company, with estimated charges of $55 million to $75 million primarily for severance. Snap plans to report its Q4 and full-year financial results soon, joining other tech giants like Microsoft, eBay, and Google in recent workforce reductions.

title: Security startup Wiz adds former Zscaler COO, plans hiring spree
summary: Cybersecurity startup Wiz has hired Dali Rajic, former COO and president of Zscaler, as its first-ever president and COO, signaling its intent for rapid growth and an eventual public offering. The company announced it reached $350 million in Annual Recurring Revenue in 2023 and plans to add 400 new employees globally in 2024. Wiz, valued at $10 billion, is also actively seeking acquisition targets in the security sector.

title: FNDX ETF: Fundamentals Are Attractive, Performance Is Not (NYSEARCA:FNDX)
summary: The Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company Index ETF (FNDX) tracks the Russell RAFI US Large Company Index and holds 730 companies, offering attractive valuation metrics and sector diversification. However, since its inception in 2013, FNDX has underperformed its Russell 1000 benchmark and several factor-based ETFs, despite its strong fundamental attributes. The article suggests that while the ETF's holdings show promise, its overall market performance has been lacking.

title: Why US large cap growth’s banner year didn’t look the same across index providers
summary: This article explains why US large-cap growth index performance varied significantly among providers in 2023, despite a banner year for the segment. The key differentiator is methodology, particularly how factors like momentum influence constituent classification, as exemplified by Meta's stock performance. Different index construction rules lead to varying index compositions and thus different returns.

title: Dollar General taps AI to optimize produce ordering
summary: Dollar General is implementing an AI and machine learning solution from Shelf Engine to enhance its fresh produce ordering and stocking processes. This strategic move aims to improve operational efficiency and ensure better in-stock levels of fresh produce at 3,000 stores by the end of the current fiscal year. The initiative follows a successful two-phase pilot in 400 stores and reflects a broader retail trend of using AI for inventory optimization and demand forecasting.

title: EA SPORTS Madden NFL 24 Predicts Kansas City Chiefs to Win Second Consecutive Super Bowl
summary: EA SPORTS Madden NFL 24 has predicted the Kansas City Chiefs to defeat the San Francisco 49ers 30-28 in Super Bowl LVIII, with Patrick Mahomes earning his second consecutive Super Bowl MVP. The prediction is part of EA SPORTS' extensive presence around Super Bowl LVIII, including community events like "Field the Future" to empower young women in football, in-game content, and the Ultimate Madden Bowl tournament. The brand is connecting sports, culture, and entertainment with various activations and celebrity performances during Super Bowl week.

title: Were Our 2023 Cloud Predictions Correct?
summary: In this article, Tracy Woo reviews Forrester's 2023 cloud predictions, evaluating their accuracy. While they successfully predicted a significant move towards cloud-native strategies, they acknowledge a notable miss regarding the adoption of third-party cloud cost management tools, underestimating the advanced DIY capabilities of sophisticated FinOps users. The author emphasizes Forrester's commitment to accountability in their predictions and hints at promising outlook for 2024 predictions.

title: What Ideas Do We Need To Change The World? 100 Issues of Socialist Alternative
summary: This article marks the 100th issue of Socialist Alternative, reflecting on their decade-long journey to provide a working-class perspective often ignored by corporate media. It highlights the consolidation of media ownership and explains how mainstream outlets fail to address issues important to working people. The piece emphasizes the newspaper's role as an "instrument of struggle," written by and for working-class individuals, to fight for a socialist world.

title: Ingles Sees Net Sales, Income Decline in Q1
summary: Ingles Markets Inc. reported declines in net sales and net income for Q1 of its fiscal 2024, with net sales decreasing by 0.8% to $1.48 billion and net income falling to $43.4 million. Despite increased operating expenses, the regional grocer managed to narrow its total debt to $546.9 million. The company asserts its financial resources are sufficient to meet future capital expenditures, debt service, and working capital needs.

title: After Earnings, Is Amazon Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar views Amazon (AMZN) stock as fairly valued after its better-than-expected Q4 earnings. The company's strong performance in AWS, advertising, and e-commerce leadership reinforces its wide economic moat. While results were good, Morningstar maintains a high uncertainty rating due to a mixed macroeconomic picture that could affect enterprise cloud spending and consumer discretionary purchases.

title: Natural Grocers Encouraged by Q1 Results, Raises 2024 Guidance
summary: Natural Grocers reported strong first-quarter earnings for fiscal 2024, with net sales increasing 7.6% to $301.8 million and daily average comparable-store sales up 6.2%. The company's {N}power rewards program also saw significant growth, reaching over 2.1 million members. Based on these positive results, Natural Grocers has raised its fiscal 2024 outlook for daily average comparable-store sales growth and diluted earnings per share, and plans to open four to six new stores.

title: JGLO Stock Price | Jpmorgan Global Select Equity ETF
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Jpmorgan Global Select Equity ETF (JGLO), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NASDAQ), and key statistics like dividend yield, expense ratio, and holdings. It also offers technical analysis over various timeframes and lists the top companies held within the ETF, such as NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon. The ETF, managed by J.P. Morgan Investment Management Inc., invests in socially conscious global developed equity markets, mirroring the MSCI World Index.

title: DLN: Large-Cap Monthly Dividend Payer Not So Hot
summary: The WisdomTree US LargeCap Dividend ETF (DLN) is rated a "Hold" due to its lower dividend yield and growth rate compared to other dividend-paying ETFs. While DLN offers monthly income and is well-diversified across approximately 300 companies, its current concentration in technology and large-cap focus present a limitation given the potential for future small-cap growth. The article suggests that while large-cap growth has dominated, changing market dynamics could favor value and small-cap opportunities.

title: Kroger links with AI retail analytics firm to boost marketplace listings
summary: Kroger has partnered with Intelligence Node, an AI retail analytics firm, to enhance product listings on its third-party online marketplace. This collaboration aims to provide clearer and more informative product descriptions, improving the customer experience and offering Kroger better insights into product performance. Intelligence Node's use of AI and machine learning, including generative AI for copy optimization, will help sellers on the Mirakl platform stand out and optimize their content.

title: Exclusive: Cisco to cut thousands of jobs as it seeks to focus on high growth areas
summary: Cisco is reportedly planning to restructure its business, which will involve laying off thousands of employees to focus on high-growth areas. An announcement could come as early as next week, ahead of its earnings call on Feb. 14. This move follows a previous restructuring in late 2022 and comes as many other tech companies are also cutting jobs.

title: Jeff Bezos sells $2 billion of Amazon shares as stock surge puts him within reach of becoming the world’s richest person
summary: Jeff Bezos sold 12 million Amazon shares worth over $2 billion this week, marking his first stock sale since 2021. This move comes as Amazon's stock surge has increased his fortune to $199.5 billion, positioning him to potentially reclaim the title of the world's richest person. Amazon had previously announced Bezos's plan to sell up to 50 million shares over the next year.

title: Vistra Corp (NYSE:VST) Surges Amidst AI Energy Boom and Nuclear Expansion
summary: Vistra Corp (NYSE:VST) has seen its stock surge over 200% year-to-date, fueled by the increasing demand for power from AI and data centers, as well as strategic expansions in nuclear energy. The company's acquisition of Energy Harbor significantly boosted its nuclear capacity, and its strong financial performance, insider confidence, and alignment with clean energy policies position it for continued growth, with analysts maintaining a bullish outlook.

title: Nvidia Overtakes Amazon in Market Value
summary: Nvidia briefly surpassed Amazon in market value, making it the fourth most valuable US-listed company earlier in the day. The chipmaker's rally, driven by exploding demand for AI chips, has seen its shares jump 46% this year. While Nvidia closed slightly below Amazon's valuation, the event marks a significant milestone fueled by the AI boom.

title: 5 Investors Betting Big on Beamr Imaging (BMR) Stock
summary: Beamr Imaging (BMR) stock surged 700% after announcing a collaboration with Nvidia to present joint research on automated video modernization at the ACM Mile-High-Video 2024 conference. The company is also launching a new video cloud service powered by Nvidia on AWS, aiming to improve video processing affordability and accessibility. While insider ownership is high, institutional ownership of BMR stock is currently very low, with only five 13F filers owning shares, the largest being Sheets Smith Wealth Management.

title: Everyone can celebrate with these post-game deals on TVs and more tech — up to 75% off
summary: Retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart are offering significant discounts on tech items, including up to 75% off, after the Super Bowl. These deals extend to big-screen TVs, soundbars, kitchen gadgets, and smart home devices. Shoppers can find projectors, smart TVs from brands like Hisense and LG, portable speakers, air fryers, and robot vacuums at reduced prices for various viewing and entertaining needs.

title: Netgear Nighthawk RS700S Wi-Fi 7 router review: Powerful, pricey and premature
summary: The Netgear Nighthawk RS700S is a powerful but expensive Wi-Fi 7 router that delivers excellent performance for existing Wi-Fi 6/6E devices and shows promise for future Wi-Fi 7 clients. However, the review advises waiting to purchase due to the current lack of widespread Wi-Fi 7 client hardware and unfinalized standards. While it's a superb piece of hardware, its high price and the immaturity of the Wi-Fi 7 ecosystem make it premature for most consumers.

title: AI frenzy puts Nvidia briefly ahead of Amazon in market value
summary: Nvidia briefly surpassed Amazon.com in market capitalization on Monday, driven by the ongoing euphoria around artificial intelligence. The chipmaker reached a record high of $734.96, giving it a market value of $1.82 trillion, slightly ahead of Amazon's $1.81 trillion. This event marks Nvidia's highest valuation relative to Amazon since 2002, with investors keenly awaiting its upcoming quarterly results on February 21st.

title: This Leveraged ETF Is Up Almost 50% the Past 3 Months
summary: The Direxion Daily Robotics, Artificial Intelligence & Automation Index Bull 2X ETF (UBOT) has seen a nearly 50% increase over the past three months, driven by strong AI-related revenue and positive future guidance from major tech companies. Nvidia, a key player in AI, is also experiencing significant growth, with its stock up about 50% year-to-date and threatening to overtake Amazon in market capitalization. Single-stock ETFs like the Direxion Daily NVDA Bull 1.5X Shares (NVDU) offer traders leveraged exposure to Nvidia's bullish performance.

title: Real Estate Giant CoStar Group Chooses Arlington for its Headquarters
summary: CoStar Group, a global real estate information and marketplace provider, is moving its headquarters to Rosslyn, Arlington, purchasing 1201 Wilson Boulevard. This move is expected to bring 650 workers to Arlington and significantly contribute to the local economy. The company's nearly $14 million payment to Arlington County for exclusive use of the Observation Deck at 1201 Wilson Boulevard will expedite the reconstruction of Rosslyn’s Gateway Park by almost a decade.

title: Machine Learning Meets Customer Experience: How AI Is Reshaping CX
summary: This article explores how artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming customer experience (CX) by enabling tailored interactions, efficient customer support, and continuous improvement through data analysis. It highlights how businesses are leveraging AI to personalize customer journeys, streamline operations with tools like chatbots, and derive valuable insights from customer data to enhance products and services. The author emphasizes that AI helps businesses adapt to dynamic market changes and stay competitive by meeting evolving customer expectations.

title: Akamai extends its edge-computing platform as it looks to challenge AWS, Azure and GCP
summary: Akamai has launched its Gecko "Generalized Edge Compute" platform, expanding its cloud-computing network with 10 new regions in Q1 and another 75 throughout the year. This initiative aims to bring compute capacity closer to users, reducing latency and enabling new use cases, directly challenging major cloud providers like AWS, Azure, and GCP. The company plans to open hundreds of small regions in the coming years and integrate its container service and automated workload platform.

title: Going Into Earnings, Is Nvidia a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar assesses Nvidia (NVDA) ahead of its Q4 earnings report, highlighting the dominance of its data center segment and the impact of AI growth. The company maintains a "Wide" economic moat due to intangible assets and switching costs, but its stock is considered overvalued with a "Very High" uncertainty rating and a fair value estimate of $480. Key factors to watch include supply constraints, U.S. restrictions on sales to China, and competition from hyperscalers developing in-house AI chips.

title: Fleet owner pleads guilty after opening sealed trailers, illegally consolidating freight
summary: A Columbus, Ohio-based trucking company owner, Gurtej Singh, pleaded guilty to wire fraud for illegally overbilling shippers and consolidating loads. Singh admitted to opening sealed trailers, removing goods, and failing to deliver many items to their final destinations, resulting in hundreds of thousands of dollars in losses for companies like Bath and Body Works and Amazon. The scheme involved altering seals and paperwork to conceal the illicit activities.

title: Shopify Fends Off Temu and Shein as Sales Narrowly Beat Estimates
summary: Shopify reported fourth-quarter sales and profit that narrowly exceeded analyst estimates, indicating successful competition against rivals like Temu and Shein. Revenue increased by 24 percent to $2.1 billion, with gross merchandise volume reaching $75.1 billion, both surpassing Wall Street projections. Despite the positive results, Shopify's shares saw a slight dip in premarket trading.

title: Steven Cohen's Point72 Asset Management Acquires New Stake in Annexon Inc
summary: Steven Cohen's Point72 Asset Management has acquired a new stake in Annexon Inc (NASDAQ:ANNX), purchasing almost 4.9 million shares, representing 6.20% of the company's outstanding shares. This investment, valued at $4.03 per share, signifies Cohen's confidence in the biotechnology firm's potential, aligning with Point72's focus on technology and healthcare sectors. While Annexon's stock has seen recent gains and has a strong balance sheet, value investors are advised to consider its low GF Score and profitability rank amidst the strategic backing.

title: BREAKING: Arlington lands HQ of another publicly traded company
summary: CoStar Group, a publicly traded real estate information and analytics provider, is moving its corporate headquarters from Washington D.C. to Arlington, Virginia. The move to the Central Place building in Rosslyn will bring 650 employees and involves nearly $5 million in state economic incentives and a $14 million payment to Arlington County for exclusive use of an observation deck. This relocation continues Arlington's streak of attracting major company headquarters.

title: Real estate giant CoStar Group moves DC headquarters across the river in new Rosslyn building
summary: CoStar Group is relocating its corporate headquarters from Washington D.C. to a newly acquired 31-story building in Rosslyn, Virginia, bringing over 600 employees to Arlington by late 2024. The move involves CoStar paying Arlington County almost $14 million for exclusive use of the building's observation deck, with these funds earmarked for the reconstruction of Rosslyn’s Gateway Park. This relocation is part of a trend of companies moving out of D.C., following Monumental Sports & Entertainment and Fannie Mae's recent announcements.

title: Nvidia replaces Alphabet as Wall St's third most valuable company
summary: Nvidia has surpassed Google-parent Alphabet to become the third most valuable U.S. company, with a market capitalization of $1.825 trillion. title: Philips and AWS collaborate to scale digital pathology
summary: Royal Philips announced an expanded collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to enhance digital pathology solutions using cloud technology. This partnership aims to improve clinical workflows, efficiently store and manage large volumes of digital pathology data, and facilitate collaboration among specialists. The initiative is set to accelerate decision-making in diagnostics, support large-scale clinical trials, and integrate AI to further advance patient care, particularly in cancer diagnosis.

title: Lilly partners with Amazon to deliver Zepbound and other drugs
summary: Eli Lilly has partnered with Amazon Pharmacy to deliver prescriptions for its direct-to-consumer service, LillyDirect, which offers drugs like the weight-loss medicine Zepbound. This expands Lilly's delivery network, previously handled by Truepill, and aims to meet the surging demand for obesity medications while ensuring proper application of financial assistance and preventing counterfeit sales. title: Sonos Era 100 review: Room-filling sound meets thoughtful improvements
summary: The Sonos Era 100 is a revamped smart speaker offering significant improvements over its predecessors like the Sonos One. It provides impressive, room-filling sound quality with enhanced stereo separation and a larger woofer. Notable new features include Bluetooth support and a USB-C port for line-in audio, making it versatile despite lacking Google Assistant and certain Trueplay advanced tuning for Android users.

title: Veritone launches AI-powered digital evidence management system
summary: Veritone has launched its new AI-powered Intelligent Digital Evidence Management System (iDEMS) to modernize digital evidence management for public safety and judicial agencies. The system extracts valuable data, automates workflows from data silos into a secure, centralized AI-driven platform, and integrates with leading industry software. Built on Veritone’s aiWARE and hosted on AWS, iDEMS centralizes digital evidence, streamlines redaction, improves analysis, and tracks persons of interest across various media types.

title: AT&T agrees to purchase carbon credits from Occidental's 1PointFive
summary: AT&T has agreed to purchase carbon dioxide removal credits from Occidental's 1PointFive as part of its goal to achieve carbon neutrality by 2035. The credits will come from 1PointFive's Stratos direct air capture facility currently under construction in Texas, which is designed to capture up to 500,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide annually. This agreement follows similar deals 1PointFive has made with other major companies like Amazon.

title: IBM Stock Gains After Cuts to Marketing and Communications Staff—Key Level To Watch
summary: IBM shares saw gains after the company announced job cuts in its marketing and communications division, part of a "workforce rebalancing" to prioritize AI and hybrid cloud skills. This move aligns with other major tech companies reducing staff amid macroeconomic uncertainties. Investors are closely watching the $206.22 level, which represents IBM's all-time high, as a potential resistance point for the stock.

title: Eli Lilly partners with Amazon to deliver GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound
summary: Eli Lilly has partnered with Amazon to distribute its GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, along with migraine medications, through LillyDirect and Amazon Pharmacy. This collaboration aims to improve patient access amid high demand and shortages for Lilly's popular GLP-1 drugs, which significantly boosted the company's recent quarterly revenue to $2.5 billion. The initiative further solidifies Amazon's presence in the healthcare sector, following previous ventures into prescription drug delivery and diabetes care.

title: Eli Lilly taps Amazon Pharmacy to help deliver weight loss drug Zepbound, other medicines to patients
summary: Eli Lilly has partnered with Amazon Pharmacy to facilitate the home delivery of prescription drugs, including the weight loss medication Zepbound, through its direct-to-consumer website, LillyDirect. This collaboration aims to enhance patient access by providing two-day delivery for Amazon Prime members and offering 24/7 access to clinical pharmacists. The move reflects efforts to streamline drug distribution and reduce consumer costs, especially as demand for Zepbound and similar drugs continues to soar.

title: Microsoft, P&G, Unilever and Walmart among 239 companies to miss net-zero deadline
summary: The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) has reclassified 239 companies, including Microsoft, P&G, Unilever, and Walmart, as "commitment removed" for net-zero goals because they failed to submit science-based targets for validation within the 24-month deadline. A significant obstacle for these companies is the difficulty in reducing Scope 3 emissions, which relate to indirect emissions from customers and supply chains. Despite the reclassification, these major corporations maintain that they are continuing to pursue aggressive emissions reduction targets and are in various stages of reviewing or updating their strategies to align with SBTi standards, with many still holding near-term validated targets.

title: Oracle unveils $10B data center expansion plan
summary: Oracle announced plans to spend $10 billion in 2025 to expand its data center capacity due to exceptionally high demand for its cloud network. CEO Safra Catz and CTO Larry Ellison highlighted the scale of these new facilities, with one U.S. AI data center capable of housing eight Boeing 747s. This expansion positions Oracle alongside other tech giants in hyperscaler data center construction, despite ongoing industry challenges like supply chain issues and lengthened buildout timelines.

summary: Bank of America’s Chief Investment Strategist Michael Hartnett believes that the current market surge in "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks and cryptocurrencies exhibits characteristics of a bubble. summary: An exchange-traded fund tracking Democratic lawmakers' stock trades has significantly outperformed a Republican-oriented fund since its launch last year, driven by strategic investments in megacap technology companies like Nvidia and Microsoft. The Democratic ETF, called NANC, has surged nearly 35%, benefiting from its tilt towards growth stocks, while the Republican ETF, KRUZ, which favors energy and value stocks, gained 18.1%. This performance gap highlights the differing investment strategies based on political affiliations and coincides with growing scrutiny over congressional stock trading.

title: Watch BofA’s Hartnett Sees Characteristics of a Bubble in Mag 7, Crypto
summary: Bank of America Corp.'s Chief Investment Strategist, Michael Hartnett, believes that the record-setting performance of the "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks and the all-time highs in cryptocurrencies exhibit characteristics of a bubble. summary: Noventiq CEO Hervé Tessler discusses the company's strategic move to list on Nasdaq from the London Stock Exchange, highlighting the benefits of increased access to capital and enhanced brand prestige. summary: NVIDIA has announced the Blackwell platform, a new GPU architecture designed to power the next generation of AI and accelerated computing. The Blackwell platform promises to enable real-time generative AI on trillion-parameter models with significantly reduced cost and energy consumption compared to its predecessor. Major cloud providers and AI companies, including Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, Tesla, and xAI, are expected to adopt Blackwell.

title: First over-the-counter birth control pill now for sale online
summary: Opill, the first oral contraceptive pill available without a prescription in the U.S., is now for sale online and will soon be in stores. Manufactured by Perrigo, the progestin-only pill costs $19.99 for a month's supply and is 98% effective when taken correctly. This marks a significant accessibility improvement for pregnancy prevention, especially for those who face barriers to seeing a healthcare provider.

summary: Gaia, Inc. has launched Gaia+, an enhanced streaming platform offering over 8,000 documentaries and series focused on transformation, spiritual growth, and consciousness expansion. summary: Copart, founded in 1982 by Willis J. Johnson, transformed from a single salvage yard into a global leader in online vehicle auctions for damaged cars, boasting a $53 billion market capitalization by March 2024. summary: The Corsair HS80 Max Wireless gaming headset is currently available at its lowest price ever, costing AU$189, a AU$90 discount from its RRP of AU$279. summary: Amazon.com Inc. has successfully defended against a patent infringement lawsuit filed by Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI) concerning its Alexa voice assistant technology. summary: UnitedHealth announced that its Change Healthcare unit has fully restored and rebuilt its cloud-based medical claims services, which were crippled by a cyberattack in February. Conversely, over 80% of households subscribe to a streaming service, with streaming revenue increasing while traditional TV revenue declined, prompting calls for regulatory changes from Canadian broadcasters to level the playing field.

summary: S&P Global Commodity Insights and Amazon Web Services (AWS) are collaborating to accelerate digital transformation in the upstream oil and gas industry. summary: POET Technologies Inc. announced its entry into the optical module market with the Wavelight™, an 800G pluggable transceiver designed for artificial intelligence and cloud data centers. summary: Costco Wholesale is expanding its partnership with online healthcare provider Sesame to offer its members access to weight-loss programs, including prescriptions for drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy. summary: Target is launching its first-ever Target Circle Week from April 7-13, coinciding with the debut of a revamped loyalty program and the return of Kristen Wiig's "Target Lady" in a new advertising campaign. Robinson, will focus on unifying commercial and sales operations, while Elkordy, with experience from Amazon, Walmart, and Chewy, will lead parcel modality enhancements.
